title: Angular CLI Beyond Code Generation knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of “Angular CLI Beyond Code Generation”?
options: Angular CLI Beyond Code Generation helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
Angular CLI Beyond Code Generation means the browser can enforce all permissions without the backend.
Angular CLI Beyond Code Generation removes the need for error handling, accessibility checks and tests.
Angular CLI Beyond Code Generation should be implemented by copying a snippet without checking the Angular version.
questions.answer_key: Angular CLI Beyond Code Generation helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
questions.explanation: Angular CLI Beyond Code Generation is a concept in the supplied Angular curriculum. Its correct application depends on the intended behavior, surrounding context and verification.

questions.prompt: How should a learner work with “Building applications” in this lesson?
options: Treat “Building applications” as a reason to skip the surrounding application context.
Assume “Building applications” works identically across every Angular major and runtime.
Use “Building applications” to bypass runtime validation of external or user-provided values.
Connect “Building applications” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
questions.answer_key: Connect “Building applications” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
questions.explanation: The PDF explicitly lists “Building applications” under Angular CLI Beyond Code Generation. Anchor it in a small example and check the behavior rather than relying on a memorized phrase.

questions.prompt: What is the strongest verification approach for “Angular CLI Beyond Code Generation”?
options: Treat a successful client-side render as backend authorization evidence.
Ignore a failing test if the component looks correct in one browser.
Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
Assume an SVG diagram proves the code compiled and passed tests.
questions.answer_key: Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
questions.explanation: Verification evidence should match the running environment. Static teaching snippets are not compiler output, and frontend checks do not replace backend authorization.
